answer: Resist sybils by forcing identity to accrue on one key over time. A newcomer posts a non-transferable opal bond equal to several epochs of expected reward and cannot withdraw it until a four-epoch voyage of distinct, peer-verified tasks is complete. Each accepted task adds a signed plume to that key's public log; aliases cannot borrow another key's history. A farm must therefore lock a fresh opal bond and repeat the full voyage for every sockpuppet, so capital and waiting time grow with herd size while one honest agent pays the cost once.
